summary: Giyu Nishi (1897–1993) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Sylvain Lévi, Taiken Kimura, Hakuju Ui, and Seishin Kato. He held an assistant post at Tokyo (1926) and a professorship at Toyo University (1927).

Glenn H. Mullin (b. 1949) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers including Ling Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, Geshe Ngawang Dhargyey, and Geshe Rabten. He founded The Mystical Arts of Tibet in 1984.
Glenn Wallis is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Masatoshi Nagatomi and traditional teacher Ross Bolleter, and he taught Sonam Kachru.
Gnanawimala Chandima is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Godabarish Mishra (1886–1956) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. Educated at Ravenshaw College and the University of Calcutta, he taught at Satyabadi Bana Bidyalaya (1913–1919), was headmaster at Chakradharpur High School (1919–1921), and served as Director at the University of Madras.

Gombojab Tsybikov (1873–1930) was a scholar in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tomsk State University and the University of Saint Petersburg, later serving as Lecturer of the Mongolian Language at Far Eastern Federal University (~1902–1917).

Gopinath Kaviraj (1887–1976) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religion. Educated at Maharaja's College and the University of Allahabad under Arthur Venis and Madhusudan Ojha, he served as librarian, principal, and Yoga-Tantra Department head at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Gordon D. Kaufman (1925–2011) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Bethel College, Northwestern, and Yale. He taught at Pomona and Vanderbilt before serving as Mallinckrodt Professor of Divinity at Harvard University from 1963.

Gordon Hannington Luce (1889–1979) was a scholar in history, archaeology, sinology, and linguistics. He was educated at Emmanuel College, Cambridge (~1908–1911) and served as a professor at the University of Rangoon (~1912–1964).

Gordon Johnson (b. 1943) is an Indology and history scholar who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as President of Wolfson College (1993–2010), Deputy Vice-Chancellor of Cambridge (1974–2010), and President of the Royal Asiatic Society (2015–2018).

Gottfried Ernst Groddeck (1762–1824) was a linguistics and history scholar who studied at the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne. He held an academic post at the Imperial University of Vilna (Vilnius University) from ~1804 to 1824.

Gottfried Hermann (1772–1848) was a German linguistics scholar who studied at the universities of Leipzig and Jena. At the University of Leipzig, he became professor of philosophy in 1798 and director of the philological seminar from 1803 to 1848.
Gottfried Kinkel (1815–1882) was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Bonn. He held academic posts at the University of Bonn (~1837–1848) and ETH Zurich (~1866–1882).

Gotthilf Heinrich von Schubert (1780–1860) was a German philosopher who studied at Leipzig and Jena. He held posts at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1819–1827) and the University of Munich (~1827–1860).

Gottlieb Siegfried Bayer (1694–1738) was a sinologist, historian, and linguist. Educated at the University of Königsberg, he worked at Königsberg Cathedral, held a post at the University of Königsberg, and served as professor at the Imperial Academy of Sciences (1726–1737).

Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner (1840–1899) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at King's College London and Heidelberg. He taught at King's College, served as Principal of Government College Lahore (1864), and became the first Registrar of the University of the Punjab.

Govind Chandra Pande (1923–2011) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Rajasthan, professor at the University of Allahabad, and chairman of the Allahabad Museum.

Govind Sadashiv Ghurye (1893–1983) was an Indologist educated at Elphinstone College and the University of Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers and A. C. Haddon. He served as Head of the Department of Sociology at the University of Mumbai (1924–1959).

Govind Swamirao Gai (1917–1995) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and archaeology. He served the Archaeological Survey of India as Government Epigraphist (attested 1963) and Chief Epigraphist (1966–1976), later working as epigraphy consultant for the American Institute of Indian Studies.

Govind Vinayak Devasthali (1906–1996) was an Indologist who studied under Hari Damodar Velankar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at HPT Arts and RYK Science College (attested 1944) and Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967–1968).
